confirmed.statement: S1 reports 120 second-year undergraduate animation students at one university in central China. All students in the three sampled classes were randomly assigned to the three conditions.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, sections 3.1 and 3.2, especially the first paragraph of Population and sampling.

confirmed.statement: The initial groups contain 40 students in GAI-SDTS, 40 in GAI, and 40 in TDL, totaling 120 randomized people.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Figure 8, the three group boxes preceding Week 1 pre-questionnaires, inspected directly; p. 4, section 3.2, establishes random assignment.

confirmed.statement: For S1-O1, Table 1 reports post-test N = 40 for each of GAI-SDTS, GAI, and TDL. Thus 40 + 40 + 40 = 120 people were analyzed in this single study, meeting criterion 2.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 1, Post-test rows and N column, independently checked with page text and PyMuPDF find_tables; p. 4, section 3.2, identifies these groups as students.

confirmed.statement: Tables 2 and 3 also report N = 40 per arm for every questionnaire outcome and subscale; they introduce no smaller analyzed sample.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Table 2, all N entries; p. 11, Table 3, all N entries; both tables checked with PyMuPDF find_tables.

confirmed.statement: The counts are individual students, not designs, ratings, sessions, or pairs: students completed the design tasks independently, and two instructors separately rated their final work.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, section 3.2, mixed-class assignment and independent task completion; p. 8, section 3.4, Instruments; p. 9, Table 1.

confirmed.statement: No exclusions or attrition are reported in the supplied document. Initial and analyzed arm counts match; there is no separate participant-flow accounting or explicit intention-to-treat claim, as the form states.
confirmed.locator: Full supplied markdown, lines 1-695; PDF p. 4, section 3.2; pp. 8-9, section 3.5; p. 9, Figure 8 and Table 1; pp. 10-11, Tables 2-3.

confirmed.statement: The paper reports one experiment. Its design-achievement outcome, questionnaires, and three pairwise contrasts concern the same cohort and must not be added as independent participant samples.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, sections 3.1-3.2; pp. 8-9, section 3.5; pp. 9-11, sections 4.1-4.3 and Tables 1-3.

confirmed.statement: Reuse of participants from another paper is not reported. Bian et al. (2025) is cited for the scoring rubric, not a shared sample; absence of cross-paper overlap cannot be established.
confirmed.locator: Full supplied document, PDF pp. 1-16; p. 8, section 3.4, first paragraph; p. 14, Data availability statement and Bian et al. reference.

confirmed.statement: The saved PDF has 16 pages, ends with references, and contains no appendix. Supplementary Table S1 is described as the design-operation sheet; its external contents could not be inspected because both retrieval routes were network-blocked.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, section 3.3; p. 14, Supplementary material; p. 16, final references. Python urllib requests to the printed Frontiers supplement page and https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1847432 both failed with WinError 10013.

summary: The PDF supports 120 people randomized and analyzed in S1, with 40 in each arm, so criterion 2 holds. No participant-count error was found; the external supplement was inaccessible and cross-paper sample overlap is not reported.
